desc.doors: Band 1, four doors: the CLI, the GitHub Action, the MCP server and the REST Core API apply the same rules and return the same envelope.
desc.core: Band 2, the Core: a stateless evaluation engine that turns an EvaluationContext into an EvaluationResult, beside the Constitution of {{corpus.adrs}} ADRs, {{corpus.rulesetPacks}} rule packs and {{corpus.schemas}} schemas, and the strip of who can say yes.
desc.suite: Band 3, Evolith Tracker: the commercial control plane that decides gates and owns state, with the five SDLC phases and their gates and the topology axis beside them.
desc.agents: Band 4, governed agents: the experimental agent runtime with {{runtime.portsDeclared}} declared port interfaces of which {{runtime.portsHot}} are on the hot path, the LLM providers a tenant chooses, and the governed-composition rail of ports, adapters and anti-corruption layers.
desc.federation: Band 5, federated governance: the Core as level 0, satellites as level 1 inheritors, and the Architecture Board approving upstream proposals.
desc.evidence: Band 6, evidence: eight generated, dated and linked tiles on how honest this picture is.

footers: Granularity = Initiatives — no tasks / backlog / epics / user-stories. Agile work items are ExternalReferenceContext ingested via ACL.

Tracker decides every phase transition · Core recommendations are non-binding (ADR-0100 · ADR-0101 · ADR-0127). CLI-only deployments block locally: evolith gate evaluate --phase · evolith phase advance.
Two planes: process governance always on (no repo needed) · architecture conformance opt-in via requiresCoreVerdict (default false).
Tracker BFF consumes the Core API as an external client — ADR-0074 explicitly rejected placing the BFF inside Core.
